newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: U.S Eximbank okays Manila nuclear power plant sale.
newsitem.headline: U.S Eximbank okays Manila nuclear power plant sale.

text.p: The Export-Import Bank of the United States (U.S. Eximbank) has approved the sale of assets of a mothballed nuclear power plant in the northern Philippines, the National Power Corp (Napocor) said on Friday.
Napocor said in a statement it is selling its entire fuel inventory and other power plant equipment from the 620-megawatt nuclear plant.

The U.S. Eximbank had extended $953 million worth of loans to the Philippine government in the early 1980s to partly finance the $2.0-billion plant which was abandoned after it was found to have some structural defects.
Under the loan agreement, the Philippines has to seek the approval of the creditor before it can dispose of the assets.
The Philippines has ruled out operating the plant as a nuclear facility and is considering converting it into a 1,500-megawatt gas-fired power plant.
The government has not yet determined when and how it would dispose of the equipment.
